interactions.title: The hobgoblin rout and safety of the Heartroot
lines: DM: And over the course of the afternoon, the hobgoblin lines break. The Rangers… harry and chase them, driving the few survivors from the valley, towards the cliff edge, only to be met by the marching Stoneborn army coming from the south, who provides the definitive final victory against the hobgoblin troops. Now, many stand and fight to the end, but many realizing their fate scatter in various directions, flee up into the mountains, flee to the north. It is… not possible to… well, not straightforward to hunt down every loose end. But… for now, anyway, for the foreseeable future, Aurbez and the Heartroot are safe.

before: Seeker: Seeker 5 RIP.
DM: Seeker 5… Yes. Seeker discovering his perfect… combat setup. Protected by a force cage.
Seeker: Always. Or nearly so.
DM: Yeah, it was great up until the wave of burning water crashed into you.

DM: So… after you defeated the Empress of Chaos, and flew back to the battle, with your… silver dragon ally, the tide of battle quickly shifted, and over the course of the afternoon, the defenders of Aurbez, the lizardfolk, the hippopotamuses, the… rangers and archers, were eventually able to not… without… at times, heavy casualties, but… many were protected by the fact that when they die in hippo form, they don't actually die, they just revert to their human form. Others by… saved by the… illusory dragon that started the battle, or the silver dragon that ended the battle.
after: DM: And so we gather, we begin, as a few… folks, rangers, and others, gather… in the late afternoon sun, as the… sun begins to sink into the sky, and campfires spring up in the… protected, sheltered valleys just south of the battlefield itself, the sort of… a place where this stream that flows through the valley of the Heartroot, meets, meets the river that… that goes on to…

DM: And… you find yourself… sitting around a campfire, the four of you. As, you know, a constant stream of visitors comes by to… congratulate and thank you to… bring you well wishes, and… a stream of food and… drink, and… thanks and gratitude.
DM: Some rangers drift through; your crew, Hektor and Marcella, reconnect.
DM: And… at this point, I mean, any… anybody you want to talk to, any… and sort of leaving a space open for any kind of… role-playing moments.

Kenzo: Kenzo actually, after the battle, I'm not sure when the right time for this, but, Kenzo wants to go back… goes back to the Heartroot, and, like… spends a bunch of time there, kinda… Yeah, just, communing with it, also, like, trying to learn more about it. Like, is it… how old is it? Like, how… what's the, you know… Kenzo's, like, very… you know, Kenzo's obviously got, got a bond with this, this—this is Kenzo's lair now, pretty soon.

lines: DM: Some rangers drift through; your crew, Hektor and Marcella, reconnect.

DM: So, so I think, I mean, I had assumed that you were gonna do that. I think maybe it would make sense for that to sort of happen as night falls, and the stars rise, and the Fox and Hunter are in the sky. And maybe all of you go talk to the Heartroot?
Kenzo: Alright, that works.
DM: You know.

interactions.title: Seeker rests beside the heroic Ladder
lines: Seeker: ((Beard maintenance)) you'll notice, if you look closely, that he's resting not against a pillow, but a different, rolled-up ropey… object, which he occasionally turns and murmurs to. The quiescent, heroic ladder.

before: Delwath: Yeah, so I mean, Delwath will certainly, like, wander around and check in on people and, you know… the… the… like, what, you know, just… what's the vibe of the camp? You know, I… it's hard to…

Delwath: I don't have a very clear sense of, like, how badly injured is the army. Is it, like, you know, half of them are dead, or is it, like, you know, how much of a disaster was this for the people?

DM: The general mood is, you know, it could have been a lot worse. You know. People died, probably… a tenth, or a… between a tenth and a… fifth of the army, but… many people didn't die who expected to die, so… while people are grieving, it's sort of like… There's an air of… you know.
Delwath: Right.
DM: There's a… there's a lot of relief and… and kinda… “we dodged a bullet” type of vibe in the camps.
after: Kenzo: In the epilogue, where's the statue of the ladder go? Where's the… Who is honoring the ladder? Where's that happening?
Seeker: Like a 10x larger than life.
Kenzo: Yeah.
DM: Statue, yeah. I mean…
Wellby: I think it's gotta be, like, historic markers, like, every place the ladder did something significant, like, gets a huge pillar, like…

interactions.title: The Rangers’ secret and Isingue’s old blessing
lines: DM: Yeah, I mean, you get a sense, and of course, most people didn't really know about the Heartroot, right? This was a secret that the Rangers kept, partly with the hope that in… in secrecy, it would be protected.

DM: But you sort of get the feeling people aren't surprised. Like, there's all these rumors, there's these stories and legends and tales of, you know, their ancestors in Isingue, and how it was this magical place of… fertile crops and… healthy people, and…

before: DM: And… for a while, it was pretty… there wasn't that, you know, weren't that many people here, they were all pretty isolated from each other. They didn't really start to become a… alliance until the War of the Ashen Horde. It was about a generation ago, maybe… maybe two generations… yeah, about a generation ago. It was 1720, so… you know. 30 years ago, roughly. And… during this war, there were…

DM: [garbled], you know, so there's ash storms that blow from the Plaguelands, often in the late summers. And… you know, make agriculture difficult, especially below the plateau. The ash storms tend to not spread super far up on the escarpment, up on this higher altitude ledge.

DM: And… during the War of the Ashen Horde, the… particularly strong ash storms spawned a bunch of… armies of some kind of ash elemental that nobody really understood how to fight or kill. And they swept through these isolated villages, and that was the sort of… what many people consider the sort of founding point of the re-founded alliance of Aurbez.

DM: And… since then, it's been… you know, pretty peaceful until now, so people have thrived, like, it's a… It's a marginal land, there's not, you know, it's hard to grow stuff, it's… hot in the summer, it's dry, there's not that much water.

DM: But… up in the mountains, it's nice. And there's… snowmelt, there's, you know. It's sort of like the Colorado Front Range in some ways. You know, lots of little streams fed by snowmelt from the… from the Sentinels, which are not, you know, just to the west of here. Pretty safe, because not much can climb… not much comes up from the… valley below.
after: DM: So, I mean, that's kind of the vibe, it's… it's… It's never been densely settled, so very lightly populated, there's no cities. The biggest city is down off the… plateau. There's a road that goes between… I mean, you would have traveled… Wellby would have traveled on the… the road that goes between Dunmar, and… and Sembara. And that road… but that road runs along the bottom of the… escarpment, for the most part, and it then cuts up to cross the passes.

DM: And the people who live in Aurbez are sort of… you know, there's people who live down along the road, right? But they're… and they're part of the alliance, right? I mean, Aursenbourg is the one city that there was the, you know, the burgher of Aursenbourg who was arguing to defend the town, but… culturally, there's… culturally, there's a lot of… you know, a much bigger Ranger presence up here. People are independent, self-sufficient. You know, kind of frontier-ish vibe.

DM: So, as… people begin to drift off from… you know, the camp, from their meal, to drop off to sleep after an exhausting day. As the stars begin to rise, you can… you can feel the pull of the… Heartroot. I mean, Kenzo explicitly can feel like it's… It's… it's… you know, it's calling for you, it's… pulling at you. Not precisely that it's, you know. It kind of feels like it's… like, you can feel… you can feel it in the back of your mind, and it's… it's there, and it's almost… just hovering at the edge of your consciousness, just… kinda waiting for you, almost.
Kenzo: Go over.
Delwath: Yeah.

interactions.title: The Heartroot stretches through its refuge valley
lines: DM: You can feel its… all of you can feel its presence. I mean, Kenzo especially. There's a vitality about the… about the valley.
Seeker: Did it relax and unfold after the combat? Yes. Because it contracted, didn't it?

DM: Yes, it's spread out, you can see it's, you know, the… it's almost like it's… when you look at it, it's sort of a mass… of roots, actually, and it's begun to… it's almost like it's beginning to stretch. Like, “ugh.”
DM: Like that, like… roots begin to spread out. You can see little, like, tendrils of vines growing, almost growing as you watch across the valley floor.
DM: There's still this sort of smell of… yeast and bread and… the air after a rain… The… the sort of…

DM: Now, actually, coming here when it's dark, you can see, actually, there's a faint, sort of, bioluminescent pulse that seems to be, like, little… little filamentous lines of… of blue-white bioluminescence that run out from this sort of mound, stretching into the soil, and light kind of running along them, and these slow pulses, almost like a very slow heartbeat.
DM: Running outward, yeah, from the sort of central area, central mound, where the Heartroot, kind of, is concentrated.
Kenzo: Are we all… like, experiencing the Heartroot in a similar way?

DM: Yeah, I mean, so Kenzo's… Kenzo's probably… more… deeply attuned to it than anybody else, having, connected with it during the battle. But yeah, you're all seeing the same things and have the same sort of… you know, sensory experience.
Seeker: Does it look like… it used to be attached to a tree or something? Like, what does it look like botanically?
DM: It looks like… mostly, like, roots, like… it's like… It's like soil that…
DM: Gather, yeah, like a root ball. And there's moss and stuff growing on top of it, but not…
DM: There's not, like, a trunk growing up or anything like that.
DM: You can see that it's kind of spreading along the edge of the val- you know, out from the sort of center. It seems to want to grow, but it's kept from doing so for some reason.

before: Delwath: Yeah.
DM: So, and… oh, actually, that reminds me, one other thing I wanted to… remind you of.
DM: It's been a while since you used a mirror, just, you know, in case that comes up and you want to use the mirror.
Kenzo: Oh, snap.

DM: So… You find yourself walking through the battlefield. And then passing into the, sort of, Heartroot Valley with the… with the stars above. Still relatively thin… moon, crescent moon… dark and peaceful and calm. As you begin to walk towards the Heartroot.
after: Kenzo: This is random, I'm not sure we've ever done this before, but, could we show the mirror the Heartroot?
DM: Yeah.
Seeker: Hmm.
Wellby: Awesome.
Kenzo: Is that an interesting thing to do? What are the other things we want to show?

interactions.title: The Heartroot’s home and history in the Mirror of the Past
lines: Kenzo: Well, before we do that, Tim, is there a sense, you know how, like, you're saying, like, it wants to spread out, but it feels like it can't? Like, I kind of sit with that resistance, like, what is resisting? What is preventing it from going where it wants to go?
DM: The… the… the stream that flows through this valley is the wrong shape.
Kenzo: Oh, yeah, I think we talked about…
DM: You always have this… you already had this sort of sense.
Kenzo: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Okay, yeah.

Kenzo: The final… well, the final mission is we need to bring it to the… we need to bring the Heartroot with us and bring it home, basically. That's kind of the… And actually, showing the mirror actually is gonna be super interesting, because it will… it will bring us back to some of the history of, like, all the weird shit, how it ended up here.
Kenzo: To be, it used to be where the, the polluted… Plaguelands.
Kenzo: Yeah, let's do it. Should we show the… let's do the mirror to the Heartroot, yeah?

DM: You take out the portable hole and slowly pull the… Mirror of the Past out. Hold it up so that the reflection of the moonlight shines onto the sort of central mound of the Heartroot. Kenzo… turns, and what is… what do you… what is the sort of question that you're using to guide your mirror visions?
Kenzo: It's like, “Tell me about your home.”
Delwath: Yeah, I was… We're on the same wavelength, so I was gonna say the same thing. Home.
Seeker: Being taken from your home, because who knows what this life story was in the long [garbled]. The thing may be very old.
Kenzo: Yeah, but it's like, “Tell me, tell the story, tell all aspects of the story of your home.” “Like, where it is, where you long to go, where you were taken from.”
Seeker: Do we want to know, like, from when you were a seed?
Wellby: Yeah, sure. Like, your whole life story.
Wellby: And, like, what do you need to flourish? Like, if we're gonna transplant it, do we just, like, drop it in the dirt somewhere, or does it…

DM: So… So you hold up the mirror. And the vision begins to shift. And it… the image flickers. And eventually settles on… just, starlit, like, you're looking from above at a starlit landscape that seems to be almost undulating like a wave, but it looks like land.

DM: And then there's this… flash of light of some kind, but it's… it registers in your eyes as almost the absence of darkness instead of bright light itself. It's… it's something like you've never experienced before. And… light begins to… shoot up, this shoot up from the center of the… of the image that you're looking at, and the land pulls apart, and then… begins to settle slowly into form.

DM: Okay, so, resuming the vision. The land splits apart, and you see this line of light shooting up. And even though you are… far away, you are also somehow close, and you see growing out of this… the sort of middle of this line that's split apart in the land, like, the same little bioluminescent, filamentous, white, multicolored lines, sort of almost crawling up out of this. And, Wellby, after you stare at this a minute, you actually… I mean, the line… this line that's being pulled apart, that's light shooting up a bit, that's somehow being formed by… reshaping of the actual physical Earth. You recognize it from maps that you've looked at, it's… exactly the pattern of the Istaros.
DM: Istaros is the river that runs past Isingue.
Kenzo: Oh, go, go ahead. Okay.

DM: So, and as you, as you watch, you can see, suddenly, this sort of riotous colors, like, washing across the landscape, and then almost a sense of… of, like, you know, multiple layers of bubbles, like, separating, right? Like, there's, you know, like, if you have two soap bubbles, right, and they pull apart like that, and many of them begin to pop. Like, it's almost you see this sort of pulling off, these, like, films of color, like, pulling off of the world that you're looking at below.

DM: Oh, meanwhile, well. You still see this… the only thing that's lit up is this… is the light shining up through the… formation of the Istaros. Meanwhile, you still see this, like, filamentous, sort of… illuminated lines begin to crawl out along… the Istaros.

DM: And after this moment of creation, the image shifts, and it rapidly… blurs through years and years and years and years. The only… still in the same perspective, the only… constant—always in the middle, always at the center point where the greatest density of these filaments were— is green, and alive. And there's, you know, winters come through, and droughts, and the land shifts, yep.

Kenzo: Like, that very first moment, where it's, like, the thing, like, cracks open, whatever, like… How old is that? Is that, like… does that feel like some beginning of time shit? Or, like, what is that?
Kenzo: So, so this is like…
DM: Like, that's like when the planes were… when the multiverse was created.
Seeker: I was wondering if that's what that was. Whoa.
Kenzo: The crown? When was the crown made?
Delwath: Or no, same time, yeah.

DM: Well, that was, like, the mythology of Taelgar, is that there was… pre… like… before the multiverse existed, all… everybody, like, all the gods just walked around the Earth. And then there was the Riving, where all the magic was segregated out into the extra… other planes, so that the material plane could exist as a real place. But there's all sorts of, like, little fragments of that moment. That's, like, the footprint of the gods that Kenzo went to in your solo adventure was also a relic of that same moment that was, like, tied to the elemental planes.
Seeker: I'm just looking at the river Istaros. We've… we've been there before. Haven't we? Isn't… is the city… The rainbow orcs on their river?
DM: It flows right past. It also is the same river that flows past Drankor.
Seeker: Oh, I didn't look down that far south. That's the same river.
DM: And, if anybody looks at a map of the Feywild, it is also exactly the path of the Sunset Gate.
Seeker: We have maps of the Feywild.
Delwath: Does anybody have a map of the Feywild?
DM: Actually, probably nobody has a map of the Feywild.
Delwath: I mean, I know what you're talking about, because I have that map of the Feywild, but I don't think it's in.
Kenzo: Well, it's like, don't make sense, because it's not, like…
Wellby: Not, you know… I'll try to guess it out.
DM: This just doesn't match one-to-one. So, 50 miles could be 1 mile or 200 miles, but it's close, right? There's features that overlap.
Kenzo: But is it still, like, the pinky bones connected to the hand bone type of thing?
DM: It's distorted, but it overlaps.

Seeker: Is the Heartroot… symbiotic, in other words, like, is the creature making up the roots themselves distinct from whatever is flowing through the glowing pulses? Like, is it a mycorrhizome situation?
DM: Well, right now, you're still watching the vision in the mirror. But, but yes, it is a mycorrhizal… myco rib… thing, situation.
DM: It's a… it's like a massive symbiotic organism that… you know, makes everything it touches grow stronger and better. And was created when… as a byproduct of the creation of the planes.
Seeker: I'm just wondering if we should try to understand it as two entities together, as opposed to one.

DM: So you keep watching in the mirror as Seeker wonders. And you see, again, this sort of… passing of the years and the seasons. Long time passing, and again, always, you know, growing and shrinking, right? But always this sort of fertile ribbon along the upper Istaros, where Isingue is, or was, still is, in ruins.

DM: And the… the image begins to drift down, closer and closer to the river itself. And you can see, as you, as you sort of drift down, as your perspective kind of zooms in, just these, these sort of… everywhere you look, right? Everywhere you look along the soil and in the dirt, there's just this richness, right? This… this thing that is now tightly constrained to, you know, really a… you know, one valley, but even less than that, right? Like, a 10 foot by 10 foot cube, and now that it's, you know, free a little bit, it's stretching out a bit. It's spreading along dozens of miles of the river and growing up from the riverbanks, and you can—you can see in the mirror the sort of vibrancy.

DM: Until… the image shifts again. You see hobgoblin, you see the city of Isingue, which is not a big city, it's… it's really mostly a town. Richly settled agricultural valleys, you know, at best. You know, think, you know, this is like, this is like, you know, Provence, or somewhere, like, fertile, I don't know what the most fertile… agricultural region of France is, but, like, that's the vibe, right? It's, like, very small… small villages, but lots of them, and… vineyards and orchards and fields of wheat, just everything rich and lush.

DM: And hobgoblins marching, large hobgoblin armies converging on the city. Fighting. The city under siege. This is like a sort of sped-up animation, and then red mist beginning to spread along the river. People dying, hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands of people dying. Fleeing in all directions.
DM: And one… stuttering image of being shaken and twisted and then grabbed carefully, and with great reverence, but still yanked out of your home.

DM: The mirror… the image in the mirror spins around, like, a dozen times, like, disorienting you. And then, you just are looking up at the sky. And you see… in the mirror, like, this sense of, like, the world shrinking around… shrinking, like, wherever… before, the visions were, like, expansive and, long and wide, right, like… seen from this great perspective, looking down on the Earth, now you're… in the sort of constrained part of the Earth, looking up at a narrow patch of sky. But the exact opposite, no sense of, like, ex… this sort of expansive growth. And no sense of, like, movement or vitality or anything.
DM: As time passes again, vision speeds up and slows down. You can see the seasons passing, you can see the sun, the days passing. But you have no real sense of… of… length.
DM: Until… you see this image stops. And you see a jade figure standing in this valley, a wizard.
Delwath: Like, Rai or somebody else?
Kenzo: Are you confused about the Jade Wizard?
DM: Looking up at the sky. And he seems to be talking… to the night sky. Well, this is presumably…
Delwath: When the… the whole thing happened, right?
DM: When what whole thing happened?
Delwath: Rai tried to clean everything up. Sorry, keep going. Sorry, sorry, sorry. Just keep going.
DM: You'll be reading his lips. Seems to have a… be having a conversation with… a friend in the sky.

DM: Talking on and on, like, you know. Rai is saying about how these, you know, he's met these monks who have also seen the… dangers of… the plague… relics, like… he thinks they'll help. Worried about trying to reach Isingue by himself, but… with their support, can be done. You know, the prison is stable, Dimitaur is watching it. We have a moment.

DM: And the voice from the sky is saying something, but there's no lips to read, so you can't hear it, but you can infer from the other half of the conversation. Worry that… the hobgoblins… might learn… too much too soon. And we better… do something, because if they uncover the secrets of Isingue, they might learn about the last… relic of the Heartroot.
DM: And then… planning for an expedition. Close the portal. A lot of discussion about a portal to Limbo, opened by Cha'mutte's death. And if there was a way to close the portal, that might help.
DM: And then the image fades. And the vision ends.

Kenzo: Wait, did I miss… like, so there was the part where, like, everything was contracting and stuff, but, like, is there… because this is from the perspective of the Heartroot, right? So… the Heartroot… did it move? Did it actually…
DM: Yeah, yeah, sorry, I… maybe that wasn't as clear as I meant it to be, so it was… somebody, you couldn't see who, fled the plague with a fragment of the Heartroot.
DM: Presumably some ranger or somebody like that.
Delwath: But wait, was the conversation with Rai taking place here?

before: Delwath: Sorry, my internet broke up right when you said your big reveal on what we should do, and then I heard you say, that was an intra- would that be an interesting thing to do? But I don't know what you said.
DM: Show the Heartroot to the mirror.
Delwath: Oh, I was thinking earlier, that's absolutely what we should do.
Seeker: [garbled].
Wellby: Let's do it.
after: Kenzo: Oh, snap.
Seeker: Whoa… Two weeks ago.
Delwath: Get Beryl to talk to us.
Seeker: Wait, did we find all of the, like, jade fingers and stuff?
DM: Yeah?

interactions.title: The Heartroot needs to reconnect to the Istaros
lines: DM: So, you know, meditating with the Heartroot and having seen this vision, I mean, you get a very clear sense that it is, in some… magical, metaphysical way, part of the river Istaros.
DM: And it is surviving here, barely.
DM: Except in the place it was created, which is the center of the upper Istaros Valley.

Kenzo: Right. But, like, even there, you know, is there, like, a… is it even more specific? Is there, like, an image of, like, a specific place? Or is it just kind of, like, throw it in the water and then everything's gonna be cool? Like, you know what I mean? Like, do we… is there any sense?
DM: No, no, no, there's not any specific… I mean, Isingue would be the specific place. That's the center of its sort of home, but… but there's nothing… you're…

DM: I mean, when you sort of meditate and commune with it, your sense is, it's, like, very eager, like… It… the river is part of it, and it's part of the river, so… And it's just been pulled… it's just been split in half.
DM: I mean, all you need to do is reconnect it, except that the river happens to be deeply contaminated at the moment.

before: Delwath: Right, of course.

Kenzo: So, okay, before we talk to Beryl, which I think we should do, just going back again to, like, the heart, so having now seen the vision, right, and understanding more about, like, kind of what happened, trauma of the heart and so on, Kenzo, Kenzo kind of, like, like, sits and… you know, with another level of understanding and… kinda, you know… greater depth of vibe with the Heartroot.

Kenzo: Wants to under… because we never really saw, you know, we were kind of asking it, oh, like, how… like, what's home? Like, how do you get home? Try to understand, like, kind of where to put it, type of thing, or, like, where we're bringing it to. Kenzo kind of, like… It's not like asking a question, but sort of, yeah, it's like leaving space for the Heartroot to, like, say more about, like, what… what is stopping it, or where does it want to be? Like, what is the… what is the… you know, and it's not…
DM: Yeah, so…
Kenzo: Anything specific, but just kind of, like, whatever the Heartroot wants to share.
after: Kenzo: Okay, so, metagame, we gotta close this portal. Portal to Limbo. Close the portal, decontaminate the river. Stick the Heartroot back in.
Seeker: And then…
Kenzo: The land is happy.
Wellby: Straightforward, right?
Kenzo: I think, right?

interactions.title: Is the ooze a cause or an effect?
lines: Wellby: ((Recalled transport and portal plan)) maybe the ooze is the cause, but maybe the ooze is an effect of something else that's going on?

before: Delwath: I mean, in fairness, this particular combat, we, like… Guerrilla warfare.
DM: You prepared for, like, two whole sessions. Yeah. To weaken the hobgoblins.
Kenzo: It was pretty brilliant. We did a good job. I'm really glad we ended up inside the centipede, by the way, in that phase. Yeah, that was awesome.
Delwath: That was it.
Seeker: Asleep, I guess, but…
